evidence.claim: China's APT export freeze and zero APT exports in January and February 2026 make APT a shared chokepoint across tungsten metal powder, WF6 semiconductor precursor gas, and cemented carbide tooling.
NDAA Section 854 becomes binding on January 1, 2027, creating a deadline-driven need for non-Chinese tungsten origin, processing, and certification.

Use SDVKY and ALM as tungsten reference anchors, not primary underfollowed alpha candidates.

tasks: For KMT, check latest 10-K/10-Q, investor presentations, segment disclosures, defense/aerospace customer language, tungsten sourcing, carbide powder exposure, and any NDAA-compliant material qualification.
For MEC.JP, verify market share, customer list, capacity, FC-BGA exposure, AI accelerator linkage, and whether copper-bonding chemistry revenue is material.
For KINSUS.TW, ATS.AT, and SHINKO.JP, verify AI accelerator FC-BGA substrate exposure, yield constraints, customer wins, and margin/utilization inflection.
For SDVKY and ALM, map whether they control APT/tungsten oxide processing or mainly upstream/captive intermediate supply.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Kennametal has secure non-China APT/tungsten oxide supply, internal APT or oxide-processing capability versus purchased feedstock, customer qualification for NDAA-compliant tungsten, and material revenue or margin exposure to tungsten powders/carbides.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Primary-source confirmation is needed on tungsten feedstock origin, degree of vertical integration, defense/NDAA qualification, and whether tungsten scarcity is material enough to affect revenue, pricing, margins, or customer allocation.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Kennametal is the best Serenity fit in this chunk because it is normally treated as a cyclical industrial tooling company, yet the tungsten squeeze thesis makes carbide powders, tungsten intermediates, wear parts, and qualified non-China supply strategically relevant. Demand is supported by industrial tooling, aerospace, energy, and possible defense procurement needs; the chokepoint is upstream APT/tungsten oxide availability. The setup is testable through filings, procurement disclosures, customer qualification evidence, feedstock sourcing, and segment margins.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: The market usually screens Kennametal under metal-cutting, industrial tools, and cyclical manufacturing rather than as a potential downstream non-China tungsten carbide and advanced-materials capacity asset. That creates a plausible hidden-signal path if customers increasingly value secure tungsten origin and NDAA-compliant supply.

If true, MEC may capture AI accelerator packaging value regardless of which substrate maker wins. It ranks below Kennametal only because the current evidence base is narrower and still needs primary-source validation of share, revenue exposure, capacity limits, and market pricing.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: MEC is likely screened as a niche Japanese chemical/materials company rather than as an AI accelerator advanced-packaging bottleneck. Its relevance is one layer beneath the visible HBM producers and substrate makers, which fits the underfollowed discovery lens.

summary: This chunk splits into two investable chokepoint maps: non-China tungsten/APT downstream scarcity and one-layer-down AI packaging materials/substrates. Highest Serenity priority goes to candidates with a real hidden supply-chain signal, public-market access, and testable evidence paths rather than the most popular names. Kennametal ranks first because it is an underfollowed industrial tooling name whose tungsten carbide and advanced-materials exposure may become strategically valuable if non-China APT/tungsten intermediate supply tightens ahead of the January 1, 2027 NDAA deadline. MEC ranks second as a possible niche AI packaging chemistry chokepoint, but evidence still depends heavily on secondary-source market-share claims. Sandvik and Almonty are useful reference anchors rather than underfollowed alpha targets. Kinsus, AT&S, and Shinko remain watch-list substrate names where the bottleneck is plausible but company-specific AI accelerator exposure needs verification.
